UN alarmed by reports that Myanmar air strike killed 50

Sept 29 (Reuters) - The United Nations expressed alarm on Tuesday at reports that an airstrike by the Myanmar military near the country's border with Bangladesh had killed 50 people and wounded dozens more, many of them critically.

A UN spokesperson said continuing violence in Myanmar's Rakhine state underscored that conditions did not currently exist for the safe return of refugees and other displaced people to Myanmar.

UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric, at a UN briefing in New York: "This latest airstrike brings that reality into sharp focus."

"The secretary-general strongly condemns the attacks and calls on all parties to end the violence immediately, to protect civilians and comply with their obligations under international law," he said, citing UN chief Antonio Guterres.

[UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk, in a statement, said the strike underlined the "grave plight faced by civilians across the country - but none more so than in Rakhine state", and: "This latest attack raises serious concerns about respect for international humanitarian law with respect to the conduct of hostilities... Under this law, warring parties must abide by the principles of distinction, proportionality and precautions in attack." Turk also called on Malaysian authorities to immediately halt the deportation of some 5,000 Myanmar nationals, which began hours after the Kyauktaw strike.]
